messages:
lex_cs: Quick heads-up for Harborline cutover tomorrow morning. Two separate oddities: (1) their privdeploy role assumption is failing with 'InvalidPrincipal' even though the role ARN matches what we asked for, and (2) our VPC endpoint for S3 in their account isn't showing any flow logs — audit team flagged missing PII access logs. Can we triage impact on go/no-go? :question:

rana_neteng: For the VPC endpoint, did they create an interface or gateway endpoint? If they used an interface endpoint we need to validate the private DNS and security group egress rules. Gateway endpoints for S3 don't show ENI flow logs, so that could explain missing entries.

omar_cloudops: Assumption error often comes from STS session tag policy or an account alias mismatch. The error example they pasted: `An error occurred (InvalidPrincipalException) when calling the AssumeRole operation: The role with name privdeploy-role cannot be found in account 334455667788` — but our operator confirmed the role exists. Could be that the role was created in a different partition or the external ID is missing.

tessa_security: Also check any IAM permission boundary on the role. If a permission boundary disallows `sts:AssumeRole` or there is an explicit Deny via SCP it will return similar messages. We should ask for the full CloudTrail event.

onboard-bot: Reminder — Harborline onboarding checklist #HB-981 close-in-24h. Please annotate any go-live blockers on the ticket.

lex_cs: I asked them to paste the CloudTrail AssumeRole event and to confirm whether they used gateway vs interface for the S3 endpoint. Proposed plan: Rana will validate endpoint type and SGs, Omar will ask for CloudTrail event and check external-id/existence across accounts, Tessa will flag any scoping issues (SCPs/permission boundaries). Can everyone ack?

rana_neteng: Ack. If it's an interface endpoint SG issue you'll see blocked TCP connections on port 443 from our subnets to the endpoint ENIs. If it's gateway endpoint, confirm whether they're relying on a NAT path that would prevent VPC Flow Logs from capturing s3 traffic. I'll post a short diagnostic command they can run.

omar_cloudops: Ack. Diagnostic ask to customer: run `aws sts get-caller-identity --profile privdeploy` from their control host and paste the ARN; share the CloudTrail event id for the failed AssumeRole. Also confirm if they use an account alias or switched master account recently.

tessa_security: Ack. If we see permission boundary restrictions, workaround for cutover: we can ask them to create a temporary cross-account role in their account allowing our Redwood operator principal (scoped to only the bucket/prefix) and expire it after 48 hours. Note this is a renewal risk note: if we need repeated temporary roles that's a governance friction we should capture in the renewal playbook.

lex_cs: Good point, Tessa. I'll add that to the renewal risk section of HB-981: "If Harborline requires operational temporary grants >2x in 90 days, flag for contract renewal conversation around managed support or dedicated capacity."

rana_neteng: Posting quick SG check snippet for customer to run in their account (paste run result to ticket):
```sh
aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters "Name=description,Values=*vpce*" --query '[].{id:NetworkInterfaceId,sg:Groups}'
```
and
```sh
aws ec2 get-flow-logs --filter Name=resource-id,Values=<eni-id>
```

If they show ENIs but no flow logs, confirm whether their flow log is to CloudWatch Logs or S3 and that the IAM role for the flow logs has the right policy.

omar_cloudops: I'll prepare a minimal temporary role CloudFormation snippet we can ask them to apply if needed. It will include an expiration tag so we can audit and remind to remove.

onboard-bot: Suggested next step — schedule 15m triage call if no response in 90 mins.

lex_cs: I'll wait for their CloudTrail and ENI output. If they don't reply we trigger the bridge. Thanks team, keeping this as a P0 for the cutover window. :white_check_mark:
